title: Bacterial wilt on Edible African Eggplant

Header: Bacterial wilt on Edible African Eggplant

Prevention: Actively remove weeds to reduce presence of alternate hosts.
Practice crop rotation with legumes, maize, onions and cabbage.
Plant in well-drained soil and avoid over watering.
Avoid injuring roots during field operations.
Use organic manure to suppress bacterial wilt pathogen.

Monitoring: Monitor the field frequently and observe for wilting and death of whole plants without yellowing or spotting.
Infected plant parts are still green but have lost turbidity.
Take direct control action when one plant is infected.
Direct Control: There are no known fungicide/bactericides for curing bacterial wilt disease of eggplant.
However, if copper based fungicides are sprayed early enough they may suppress the infection.
Prune affected plant parts and destroy by burning or deep burying.
Restrictions: PHI 7 days, toxic to aquatic organisms.
